clue.text: Formidable woman writer produces cheese

blocks.note: a gorgon is a fearsome, forbidding woman, after the Medusa of myth
Emile Zola, the French novelist

explanation.surface: A fierce woman author turns out a cheese, as if writing were dairy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese, named after a town near Milan.

clue.text: Cook too much throughout party

blocks.note: over as in 'all over', throughout
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Someone keeps overcooking the food all through a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo food is to leave it on the heat too long, a common kitchen verb.

clue.text: Folklorist set out to be most forbidding

indicators.note: something put out of place is disturbed, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: either of the Brothers Grimm, collectors of German folk tales
these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collector of folk tales sets out to be as forbidding as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means stern and forbidding in manner, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Old PM - one paid to dismiss a Geordie, say

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the named letter is removed from the word before

blocks.note: Lord North, British prime minister during the American War of Independence
someone who is paid earns money
the letter to be removed, taken as written

explanation.surface: An old prime minister sacks a worker from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: EARNER drops its A to leave ERNER. A Geordie is a person from Newcastle upon Tyne, in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Tyneside comes from the north of England, so is an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Oppressive emperor in old country

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
the Roman emperor Nero
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A tyrannical emperor rules some ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous describes a burden that weighs heavily, matching oppressive as a near synonym.

clue.text: The last word in top-class soldiers

blocks.note: A as in A1 or grade A, the top class
men, ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Elite troops have the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer, quite literally the closing word spoken.

clue.text: Rate poet fiddled for work performed on stage

indicators.note: something fiddled has been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A poet of some standing cheated to get a piece put on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light comic opera, a musical work staged in a theatre.

clue.text: Medium covering a Prom broadcast in mundane manner

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so one word goes outside the others
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the telly, television, is a broadcast medium
these letters are rearranged before going inside

explanation.surface: The television is showing a Promenade concert on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a BBC summer concert season in London, regularly televised.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means of worldly rather than spiritual things, so temporally is in an earthly, mundane way.

clue.text: Bird identified by ring hit by mediocre shot

blocks.note: first meaning: a black and white bird of the crow family
second meaning: in target shooting, a hit in the outermost but one ring

explanation.surface: A bird is recognised by a ring on its leg, as birdwatchers do.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringing birds sounds like ornithology, but the ring is on a shooting target.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a common crow-family bird and the target-shooting term for a shot striking the second outermost ring.

clue.text: Previous record of a top boxer, say

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a purebred animal

blocks.note: first meaning: a history or ancestry, a track record
second meaning: a purebred animal, the boxer being a dog breed

explanation.surface: We look at the past fight record of a leading boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not a fighter; a top show dog is a thoroughbred.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigree means lineage or background, and also an animal of recorded pure breeding.

clue.text: Messenger on horseback - second to reach the post

blocks.note: a runner carries messages
a jockey who is up is mounted and riding

explanation.surface: A mounted courier comes second in delivering the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The post sounds like mail, but it is the winning post of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up finishes second, the one who crosses the line just after the winner.

clue.text: Left between midnight and an hour later

definitions.text: between midnight and an hour later

blocks.note: first meaning: departed

blocks.clueFragment: between midnight and an hour later
blocks.note: second meaning: as in '... twelve', past the stroke of the hour

explanation.surface: Someone slipped away in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone means departed, and 'gone midnight' means just past twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Armed man appears to hang around after bar's held up

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means lifted so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the snug is a small cosy bar in a British pub
to linger is to hang around

explanation.surface: A man with a gun loiters after a bar is robbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' suggests an armed robbery; here it flips SNUG upwards. 'after' places the loitering word second.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger is a Wild West gunfighter, a man who carries and uses a pistol.

clue.text: He speaks clearly and freely in an English court

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so these letters can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness speaks openly and clearly in an English courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' looks like it describes how he speaks, but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enunciate is to pronounce words distinctly, so an enunciator is a clear speaker.

clue.text: Peevish type's plot holds up trial

blocks.note: a cross is a burden or trial to bear
a patch of ground, a plot

explanation.surface: A grumpy person's scheming is delaying a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'holds up' means the plot sits beneath and supports the trial, so the trial comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an old-fashioned name for a bad-tempered, irritable person.

clue.text: A lot of new fleece for homemaking

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written, before shortening
to fleece or sting is to swindle

explanation.surface: Plenty of fresh wool for the household.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleece looks like wool, but it is the verb to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting is a bird building its home, and also the urge to set up a household.

clue.text: Giving away recent purchases

blocks.note: first meaning: informing on someone, British slang to shop a person to the police
second meaning: the goods just bought

explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for betraying them, and the noun names goods just bought in stores.

clue.text: It may be needed on ship, as pilot ordered

definitions.text: It may be needed on ship

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are sorted anew

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something is required aboard, as the pilot has commanded.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest sail on a mast, standard rigging aboard a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Outline for players put in a score as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Musicians receive a sketch to be worked into the arranged score.
explanation.walkthrough: The players and the score suggest musicians, but the players are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the plot outline of a play or film, a sketch of the action for actors.

clue.text: Polish workers possibly become more powerful

blocks.note: worker bees, so workers might be these insects
to wax is to grow in strength, as the moon waxes

explanation.surface: Workers from Poland may grow in strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it is the substance for shining furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswax is used as a furniture and floor polish, applied to wood for shine.

clue.text: Is she invariably spotted as well as her mate?

definitions.text: Is she invariably spotted as well as her mate?

blocks.clueFragment: Is she invariably spotted as well as her mate?
blocks.note: surface reading: is this woman always seen out in public alongside her partner?
setter's reading: a female big cat whose coat is patterned with spots, just like her male partner's

explanation.surface: Gossip asks whether a woman is always seen with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted means marked with spots, and a leopard never changes its spots, hence 'invariably'.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the leopard is a spotted big cat, just like the male.

clue.text: Child's play some criticise as youthful

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the answer sits within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the ends and starts of these words

explanation.surface: Some people sneer at children's games as immature.
explanation.definitionFit: Child's play is an idiom for a task so simple a child could do it.

clue.text: Tried hard roe initially put in oven

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
to put something in is to place it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a stove is an oven
the first letter of roe

explanation.surface: A cook tried hard to get the fish eggs into the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to make great efforts.

clue.text: Unusually plain suit - one put out for wedding

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so these letters are shuffled
put out means removed, so the letter for one is taken away

blocks.note: the letters before removal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A simple outfit is rejected for the wedding, unusually.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a wedding ceremony or marriage.

clue.text: Book used for parts of play

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... of the Apostles in the New Testament
second meaning: the main divisions of a drama

explanation.surface: A script is divided into sections for staging.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book is called Acts, and a play is divided into acts and scenes.

clue.text: Trains here for battle

blocks.note: first meaning: a major London railway terminus
second meaning: the 1815 defeat of Napoleon

explanation.surface: An army drills in this place ahead of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Trains looks like a verb for soldiers drilling; it is the railway noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is a London mainline station and the Belgian site where Wellington beat Napoleon.

clue.text: Song thrush initially observed by bird man

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each of these words gives its opening letter
being observed by something means it comes after, so these letters follow the next piece

blocks.note: the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes a song thrush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird man' suggests an ornithologist, but bird and man are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Cub Scout leader seizing young sucker's gun

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a sixer leads a six, a small group of Cub Scouts
a sucker is a shoot growing from a plant's root, here a young one

explanation.surface: A Cub leader grabs a young child's toy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Sucker looks like a gullible person, but it is a botanical shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-shooter is a revolver holding six rounds, a type of handgun.
